title: census.py repin plans each source from the facts and anchors read once, so a fact citing two pinned sources loses its anchor after the first is re-pointed
goal: cmd_repin in _tools/census.py re-reads the facts and anchors after each re-point (the one read before the loop at census.py:2399 goes), so a second pinned source cited by the same fact still finds its anchor in the same run, and --dry-run prints the same outcome as the real run.

run: import sys; s=open('_tools/census.py').read(); sys.exit(1 if 'facts, anchors = factdiff.cited_facts(), factdiff.read_anchors()' in s else 0)

repro_reason: found by reading census.py cmd_repin in the SP-ilje65fa review; no kb fact today cites two pinned sources that both qualify, so the repro reads the single read of facts and anchors before the loop
notes: Premise (2026-10-14, ae319c43c5, by reading; no kb fact triggers it today): census.py:2399 reads facts and anchors once, :2461-2468 re-keys anchors in memory to the reworded fact's new key while facts keep the old key, so a second pinned source's repin_plan misses its anchor; --dry-run never re-keys. Goal narrowed at planning to the re-read fix, so the repro (the single read line) is sound for it; the behaviour is proved by extending census_repin_writes_the_new_row_only_when_every_cited_fact_is_word_for_word_at_the_newer_commit (test_redact.py:1444) with a fact citing two pinned sources that both end superseded in one real run, the dry run's count equal to the real run's; no new id.
